description.value: The study investigated how perceptual decision variables and confidence are represented in the human brain during visual motion discrimination, and whether decision-variable signals in cortical regions are linked to confidence signals in the ventral striatum.

design.value: Participants performed a visual random-dot motion discrimination task during fMRI. On each trial they reported the dominant motion direction and then rated confidence continuously; fMRI data were analyzed with mass-univariate GLM, multivariate searchlight classification, multivariate searchlight regression, and multivariate connectivity analyses.

description.value: Subjects indicated their confidence by moving a white dot with a trackball to the part of a continuous confidence bar corresponding to their confidence. The scale ranged from “very sure about the direction of motion” to “no idea at all.”

source_definition.value: A binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion of the stimulus, “motion up” or “motion down.”
The direction of motion presented by the random dot motion stimulus, upward or downward.
Confidence ratings were divided into 3 confidence bins by separating each subject’s ratings at the 33.3 and 66.6 percentiles: “low,” “medium,” and “high confidence.”
A parametric modulator reflecting the linear increase or decrease in BOLD signal across different confidence levels.

A proxy of the difference between the internal decision variable and the criterion, constructed on each trial by multiplying the binary choice, coded as -1 or 1 for “up” and “down,” by the binned confidence rating, coded as 0.5, 1.5, and 2.5.

levels.value: Labels ranging from -2.5 to 2.5, corresponding to “choice down, high confidence” through “choice up, high confidence”

source_definition.value: Response time was used as the first parametric regressor when testing confidence-related responses after accounting for response time.
Missed trials were modeled in a separate regressor.

description.value: Nineteen young and neurologically healthy subjects took part in the study; one participant was subsequently excluded due to excessive head motion, leaving 18 subjects (6 female, 1 left-handed, mean age 26.4 years, SD 3.4).

task_description.value: Subjects observed a random dot motion stimulus and performed two consecutive responses: a binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion and a confidence rating of that judgment on a continuous scale. In the main experiment, motion coherence was fixed to each subject’s individually calibrated 75% threshold.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to indicate the perceived direction of motion by pressing the button corresponding to the chosen stimulus direction, to respond even when very unsure, and to indicate confidence from “very sure about the direction of motion” to “no idea at all.” They were instructed not to restrict judgments to only a small portion of the confidence scale unless confidence truly did not fluctuate.

stimuli.value: A random dot motion stimulus was presented for 1 s. It contained 500 dots in a circular annulus within a 10 × 10 dva square region; signal dots moved upward or downward at 2.5 dva/s, noise dots moved in equally spaced directions, and each dot had a limited lifetime of 200 ms.

task_description.value: A functional localizer run was used to locate motion-sensitive region MT+/V5 in each individual subject.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla TIM Trio MRI (Siemens) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: An anatomical scan was acquired for inter-subject normalization and mapping of functional to reference structural images. The scan was a T1-weighted MPRAGE volume with TE 2.52 ms, TR 1900 ms, flip angle 9°, FOV 256 mm, matrix size 256 × 256, slice thickness 1 mm, and 192 slices.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla TIM Trio MRI (Siemens) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: T2*-weighted gradient-echo echo-planar images were acquired. In total, 2247 functional volumes were acquired per subject, corresponding to the experimental runs and the functional localizer. The first 2 functional volumes were automatically discarded in each run to allow for T1 equilibrium effects.

Functional images were spatially realigned and slice-timing corrected. For the univariate analysis they were spatially normalized using subject-specific transformation matrices and smoothed with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. For both multivariate analyses, functional data were not spatially warped or smoothed. A template structural reference image was created using DARTEL and brought to MNI space using affine transformation; a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter was applied to the univariate data.

steps.value: Creation of a template structural reference image using DARTEL
Affine transformation of the template to MNI space
Spatial normalization for the univariate analysis
6 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing for the univariate analysis
No spatial warping or smoothing for the multivariate analyses

model_settings.value: A GLM with 10 regressors per run modeled a 2-s RDM stimulation regressor, a parametric confidence regressor, missed trials, six head motion regressors, and a constant term. The stimulation and missed-trial regressors were convolved with an HRF. Confidence was entered as the second parametric regressor; response time was entered first in the control analysis. Group-level positive and negative relationships were tested with t-tests at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

estimator.value: SPM8 GLM estimation followed by group-level t-tests

model_settings.value: Choice classification was performed separately for the two stimulus motion directions using GLM parameter estimates, a 10-mm-radius searchlight containing 139 voxels, and a leave-one-run-out cross-validation scheme. Ten pattern vectors were classified with a linear SVM using standard cost c = 1. The two motion-direction maps were averaged, transformed to MNI space, smoothed for group-level analyses, and tested against 50% chance.

estimator.value: leave-one-run-out cross-validated linear support vector classification

model_settings.value: A 10-mm-radius searchlight was analyzed using 30 pattern vectors representing six decision-variable regressors per run. A linear nu-SVR was used with nu = 0.5 and cost c = 1, with leave-one-run-out cross-validation. Predictive accuracy was the Fisher-z-transformed correlation between true and predicted labels, and the results were masked by regions carrying choice-related information.

estimator.value: leave-one-run-out cross-validated linear nu-support vector regression

model_settings.value: For each candidate seed region, predicted decision-variable labels were transformed into predicted confidence values and correlated across runs with predicted confidence values in the ventral striatum. Searchlights had a 10-mm radius. Significance was assessed with 120 possible run permutations per subject and Bonferroni correction across 12 regions.

name.value: Negative parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: negative linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs

interpretations.value: brain regions displaying a negative relationship with confidence

definition.value: classified choices based on brain signals, separately for both directions of motion, independent of the direction of motion of the stimulus

interpretations.value: brain regions in which activity reflected the subjects' choices

name.value: positive parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: positive linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs

interpretations.value: activity in the ventral striatum reflected the degree of perceptual confidence

title.value: Brain regions where activity is related to confidence

caption.value: A complete list of brain regions with parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence.

footer.value: The coordinates and z-values refer to the peak within each cluster. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: Reports brain regions showing parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence.

title.value: Brain regions informative about the DV

caption.value: Brain regions carrying information about the DV reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings.

footer.value: Mean Fisher z-values reflect the z-transformed size of the correlation between predicted and true values in the multivariate regression analysis. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: Reports brain regions carrying information about the decision variable reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings.
